title: Beginning
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
<<set $tutorialInvestigate to false >>
<<set $unfadeBlack to false >>
"…"
"………"
[spacing=5]BZZT–![/spacing]
[i]A loud, unfamiliar alarm jolted me awake, my eyes blinking to adjust to the dimness.[/i]
<<set $unfadeBlack to true >>
“What was that alar—"
"...Huh?”
[i]I look around, dumbfounded.[/i]
“Just where the hell am I…”
“This is so not where I last remember falling asleep.”
“Urgh–!”
[i]I put a hand to my head, the beginnings of a headache forming.[/i]
“What… is going on..?”
[i]Panic sets in, my heart racing.[/i]
[i]I was just at home a minute ago, wasn’t I?[/i]
[i]At my desk, writing this godforsaken report on myths of mermaids, sirens more specifically, and I just. Took a nap.[/i]
[i]And now I’m here, wherever “here” is.[/i]
“O-Oh god, am I kidnapped?”
[i]I looked around at my surroundings again, but it only left me in a daze as confusion began to replace panic.[/i]
[i]This space… Certainly doesn’t feel like where you would keep a hostage.[/i]
[i]Rather it feels more like a very large fish tank?[/i]
“Either way… I need to get out of here.”
[i]I have no idea who brought me here, and why, but from my long history of watching mystery anime, there’s always a reason for everything.[/i]
[i]...Aaaand the reason I’m here now probably isn’t good.[/i]
“Ugh… Escape first, think later!!!”
spacerrrrrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>
<<set $tutorialInvestigate to true >>

title: Tutorial/Investigate
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
Hi. Congratulations, [b]YOU[/b] need to figure out how to escape.
To do so, turn around by using the [b]left and right arrow keys[/b].
Since this is a very limited and cramped space, you can only go forward a little, using the [b]up arrow key[/b], to more closely inspect the area.
To inspect anything of interest, [b]hover[/b] over the object with the [b]cursor[/b] and [b]click to interact[/b].
Some objects you can [b]focus[/b] on more closely, and you can use the [b]left and right arrow keys[/b] to turn around and inspect it.
To exit [b]focus[/b], use the [b]down arrow key[/b].
Tutorial over, good luck!
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>
<<set $tutorialInvestigate to false>>

title: BlueCoral
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]Some blue coral. It looks kind of spiky.[/i]
[i]What if I broke off a part and sharpened it like a pickaxe, and dug my way out of here…[/i]
“...Yeah, that’s probably wishful thinking.”
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: OrangeCoral
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]Some orange coral. If it was thinner, denser, maybe it would have looked like instant noodles before it was cooked…[/i]
[i]...Am I just hungry?[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Seaweed1
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]These seaweed are straight upright… They’re probably fake.[/i]
[i]I cautiously reach out to touch it.[/i]
“...”
[i]Ew— it feels a bit slimy, but definitely rubbery. And fake.[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Seaweed2
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]These seaweed plants look sturdy enough. Maybe it can be used as rope???[/i]
[i]Uh, rope for what though.[/i]
[i]Mysteriously shrunken boy from hit mystery anime, you’re failing me here.[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Rocks/BeforeTimer
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
“Rocks, huh, reminds me of my lost pet rock, Rocky…”
[i]…Hang on, that’s irrelevant right now.[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: TrapdoorLock/Inspection1
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
<<set $lockFocus to false >>
<<set $trapdoorFocus to false >>
<<set $inspectionEnd to false >>
“Wait, that’s—!”
spacerr
<<set $lockFocus to true >>

title: BrokenTimer/NoRock
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
“Is this a digital timer? What’s this doing here?”
[i]It looks like… it’s broken.[/i]
“But then why is it here…”
[i]I examine the random timer, trying to see if I can take it off the wall.[/i]
“Ugh!—”
[i]No dice. The timer is screwed tightly to the wall, but the display lid seems a bit loose.[/i]
“No matter how random, everything has a purpose… Let’s break this open!”
[i]Uhh… With what, though. Maybe I could find a heavy object to smash it open somewhere?[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: BrokenTimer/YesRock
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
"It's open!"
"Wait, what is that?"
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: OxygenPump/Front
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]…What the heck is this?[/i]
[i]It looks like a container or a case of some sorts.[/i]
“If we’re going with a fish tank theme, could this be an oxygen pump box?”
[i]Since I haven’t died due to a lack of oxygen while unconscious, maybe this is why?[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: OxygenPump/Side
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]There seems to be a starshaped imprint here.[/i]
“This reminds me of those high tech fancy hand imprint locks…”
spacerr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]This rock is too small.[/i]
spacerr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
“..?”
[i]This rock isn’t budging!![/i]
[i]Has it been mysteriously superglued down or something?[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]This rock seems just right for smashing the timer open![/i]
spacerr

title: Tutorial/Inventory
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
Oh, I forgot to tell you!
With the cursor, some useful objects can be picked up by clicking on them.
They will be stored in your inventory, which you can access by pressing the [b]key 'X'[/b]. 
Try pressing [b]'X'[/b] now to open your inventory.
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Tutorial/InventorySelect
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
<<set $inventoryTutorialHeldItems to false >>
This is your [b]inventory[/b]!
You can see all the objects you have picked up in here.
If you have multiple items, use the [b]up and down arrow keys[/b] to select an item on the right sidebar.
You can turn and rotate your selected item by clicking on the [b]left and right arrows[/b] to view different angles of it.
To inspect an item, [b]click[/b] on the item.
To quit your inventory, either press the [b]key 'X'[/b], or click the [b]exit button[/b] on the [b]top left[/b].
spacerrrr
<<set $inventoryTutorialHeldItems to true >>
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Starfish/BeforeOxygenPump
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]Ooo starfishes.[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Starfish/AfterOxygenPump
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]Hm... Could this be a part of a puzzle?[/i]
"Let's keep it handy for now..."
spaccerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: TrapdoorLock/Dials
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
“There’s dials with symbols on them, so it’s a combination lock?”
[i]I attempt to turn them, but the dials don’t budge.[/i]
“..? A combination lock with dials that don’t move… How useful…”
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: TrapdoorLock/Locks
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]Is this another lock? It has a weird design for a lock…[/i]
“Hm… there’s a rectangular hole here. Maybe a key could be inserted?”
[i]Rectangular keyholes are a bit unusual though...[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: TrapdoorLock/SummaryInspection
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
[i]So, there’s dials that probably form a combination, and there’s two locks that need keys on top of that.[/i]
[i]The keys probably unlock the restriction on the dials.[/i]
“Just who created this lock…”
[i]If I want to escape and leave I have to find the keys first and then figure out the combination. [/i]
[i]…Based on my escape room experiences, the keys are probably hidden somewhere in this space.[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: TrapdoorLock/Inspection2
body:
<<set $lockFocus to false >>
[i]It looks like a combination lock.[/i]
“And where there’s a lock, there’s something important…”
spacerrr
<<set $trapdoorFocus to true >>

title: TrapdoorLock/Inspection3
body:
<<set $trapdoorFocus to false >>
“Is this the exit?”
[i]I glance at it suspiciously, and mull over it.[/i]
“Why is the lock placed here so intentionally… Almost whoever brought and trapped me here wants me to get out?”
[i]I shake my head.[/i]
“Ugh, I can figure out their intentions after I leave here.”
[i]Let’s try examining that lock again.[/i]
spacerrr
<<set $inspectionEnd to true >>
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Shells
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
"A shell?"
[i]Suspicious, I picked it up.[/i]
[i]...There's something on the back of it! I should take a look closer at it.[/i]
spaccerrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>

"A key..."
[i]It will definitely be handy for getting out of here, let's keep it for now.[/i]
spaccerrrrrrrrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

body:

[i]A key! It was locked behind this case, so it must be important. Let's keep it for now.[/i]
spaccerrrrrrrrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>

title: Tutorial/InventoryHeldItems
body:
<<set $dialogueEnd to false >>
One last thing! At the top left corner, you can which item you have in hand.
What you currently have in hand will be the [b]selected item inside your inventory[/b].
So, to [b]switch[/b] the item in your hand, [b]open your inventory[/b] and select another item.
If you have an item in hand, you can use it by [b]clicking[/b] where you want to use it on.
That's all, good luck!
spacerrrr
<<set $dialogueEnd to true >>
